sentences.en: So loop fusion is when you take multiple loops and you combine them into a single loop.
sentences.zh: 循环融合是指将多个循环合并为一个循环。

sentences.en: And loop fission is when you take a single loop and split it into multiple loops that iterate over the same index range as the original loop.
sentences.zh: 循环拆分是指将一个循环拆分为多个循环，这些循环遍历与原始循环相同的索引范围。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast episode 51, recorded on November 5th, 2021.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 51 期，录制于 2021 年 11 月 5 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we talk about the difference between efficiency and speed.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 将讨论效率与速度之间的区别。

sentences.en: Now, listener, strap in for Bryce's explanation of the difference between efficiency and speed.
sentences.zh: 那么，听众朋友们，请系好安全带，听听 Bryce 对效率和速度区别的解释。

sentences.en: And I'll give a little 30-second intro.
sentences.zh: 我会先做一个 30 秒的简短介绍。

sentences.en: A couple episodes ago on, I think it was the combinatory logic episode,
sentences.zh: 在几期节目之前，我想是在组合逻辑那一期，

sentences.en: I was saying how if you fuse, you know, two algorithms into one using combinators,
sentences.zh: 我说过，如果你使用组合子将两个算法融合为一个，

sentences.en: you're going to end up with faster code because doing a minimum element and maximum element separately
sentences.zh: 你最终会得到更快的代码，因为分别计算最小值和最大值，

sentences.en: versus, you know, min-max element, which Ben Dean very, you know, astutely pointed out that,
sentences.zh: 与计算最大最小值相比——Ben Dean 非常敏锐地指出，

sentences.en: you know, you're never actually going to match that because the performance of min-max element has three over two N operations, which a fused one is still going to have two N.
sentences.zh: 你实际上永远无法与之相比，因为最大最小值算法的操作次数是 1.5 倍的 N，而融合后的算法仍然是 2 倍的 N。

sentences.en: But anyways, that's besides the point.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，这题外话了。

sentences.en: But thank you, Ben, for clarifying that.
sentences.zh: 不过还是感谢 Ben 的澄清。

sentences.en: Bryce pointed out that, like, well, it'll be twice as efficient, but not necessarily twice as faSt.
sentences.zh: Bryce 指出，嗯，它会更有效率，但不一定速度更快。

sentences.en: And in that episode, I don't think, I think in listening back to it, I don't think I fully grokked what Bryce meant by that.
sentences.zh: 在那一期节目中，我想回听的时候，我觉得我并没有完全理解 Bryce 的意思。

sentences.en: So now enter Bryce with his elaboration on efficiency versus speed.
sentences.zh: 所以现在有请 Bryce 对效率与速度进行详细阐述。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I like to think of this as, I'm not surprised that we are coming at this from different angles because I think you are much more of a theorist, a pure computer scientist,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样思考，我不惊讶我们从不同的角度来看待这个问题，因为我觉得你更像是一个理论家，一个纯粹的计算机科学家，

sentences.en: whereas I am much more of a software engineer.
sentences.zh: 而我更像是一个软件工程师。

sentences.en: And maybe that's even, like, too haughty a title, like a software plumber.
sentences.zh: 也许这个头衔还有点太高大上了，就像个软件管道工。

sentences.en: You know, I sort of come at it from, like, the grounds up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有点从底层开始考虑。

sentences.en: Like, how does this thing actually run and work in production?
sentences.zh: 比如，这个东西在生产环境中到底是怎么运行和工作的？

sentences.en: Whereas you're much more the person to think about, you know, the whiteboard solution.
sentences.zh: 而你更多是那种考虑白板方案的人。

sentences.en: And that's not meant as a dig.
sentences.zh: 这并不是为了挖苦你。

sentences.en: It's a little bit of a dig.
sentences.zh: 确实有一点点挖苦。

sentences.en: A little bit of a dig.
sentences.zh: 有一点点挖苦。

sentences.en: But so let's start off with an argument that I know you will find compelling because I've made it before, which is the question of efficiency when it comes to paralyzation.
sentences.zh: 但让我们从一个我知道你会觉得有说服力的论点开始，因为我以前提过，那就是并行化时的效率问题。

sentences.en: So we've told this story a few times on the podcast, but once on a drive from the south San Francisco Bay up to San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我们在播客里讲过几次这个故事，有一次在从旧金山湾区南部开车去旧金山的路上，

sentences.en: I explained to Connor how you could paralyze an inclusive scan.
sentences.zh: 我向 Connor 解释了如何并行化包含扫描（inclusive scan）。

sentences.en: And the reason that Connor thought that it could not be paralyzed is because Connor was thinking about paralyzing the most efficient version of a scan algorithm.
sentences.zh: Connor 认为它不能被并行化，是因为他当时在考虑如何并行化最高效的扫描算法版本。

sentences.en: And I explained to him how you could implement a parallel scan that is work inefficient.
sentences.zh: 我向他解释了如何实现一个工作效率较低的并行扫描。

sentences.en: That is, it's less efficient.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它的效率较低。

sentences.en: It does more operations than a serial scan.
sentences.zh: 它比串行扫描执行了更多的操作。

sentences.en: But it doesn't matter that it does more operations because they can be done in parallel.
sentences.zh: 但它执行更多操作并不重要，因为这些操作可以并行完成。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you do N work in serial for some algorithm and you can paralyze it and, you know, paralyzing it means that you actually end up doing two times N work,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对某个算法进行 N 次串行工作，而你可以将其并行化，并且并行化意味着你最终做了 2 倍 N 的工作，

sentences.en: that might be perfectly okay because if your goal is, you know, to get an answer faster, it doesn't matter if you're doing more work if that work can be done quicker
sentences.zh: 这可能完全没问题，因为如果你的目标是更快地得到答案，那么如果这些工作能更快完成，做更多的工作也无所谓，

sentences.en: because it's being done across multiple threads.
sentences.zh: 因为它们是在多个线程上同时完成的。

sentences.en: So you understand that argument, yes?
sentences.zh: 所以你理解这个论点，对吧？

sentences.en: You understand that in the case of, you know, thread parallelism, you know, being inefficient might be faster.
sentences.zh: 你理解在线程并行的情况下，效率较低可能反而更快。

sentences.en: Correct, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: 100% on board.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: But the thing is, that applies to, like, almost every case that we encounter in the field because even when you're programming for a single thread,
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这几乎适用于我们在实践中遇到的所有情况，因为即使你是在为单线程编程，

sentences.en: the hardware that you are running on is still actually parallel under the hood.
sentences.zh: 你运行的硬件在底层实际上也是并行的。

sentences.en: You know, there is a part of your processor that loads data.
sentences.zh: 你知道，处理器中有一部分负责加载数据。

sentences.en: There's a part of your processor that fetches instructions, that decodes instructions.
sentences.zh: 有一部分负责获取指令，解码指令。

sentences.en: There's a part of your processor that does adds.
sentences.zh: 有一部分负责执行加法。

sentences.en: There's a part that does multiplies, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 有一部分负责执行乘法，等等等等。

sentences.en: And those parts can run in parallel.
sentences.zh: 这些部分可以并行运行。

sentences.en: And so on every modern processor, your single-threaded code is actually being paralyzed under the hood at a level that you don't really see
sentences.zh: 因此在每台现代处理器上，你的单线程代码实际上在底层是以你无法察觉的程度被并行化了，

sentences.en: in that the actual things that need to happen to make that serial thread,
sentences.zh: 因为为了使那个串行线程真正运行所需的实际操作，

sentences.en: you know, the serial set of operations that you want to do to make that actually execute,
sentences.zh: 也就是你想要执行的一系列串行操作，

sentences.en: those things don't strictly happen in order, and some of them are overlapped and asynchronous.
sentences.zh: 这些操作并不严格按顺序执行，其中一些是重叠和异步的。

sentences.en: And so then again, we get to this idea that in some cases,
sentences.zh: 所以我们又回到了这个观点：在某些情况下，

sentences.en: things that are less efficient might actually be faster because efficiency isn't really our goal.
sentences.zh: 效率较低的东西实际上可能更快，因为效率并不是我们真正的目标。

sentences.en: Our goal is time to execution.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是执行时间。

sentences.en: So let's move on to this particular case of loop fusion and loop fission.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们继续讨论循环融合和循环拆分这个特定案例。

sentences.en: Do you know what those terms mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道这些术语是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: We'll pretend for the sake of the listener that I don't know what loop fission is because this is the first time we are recording this.
sentences.zh: 为了听众着想，我们就假装我不知道什么是循环拆分，因为这是我们第一次录制这个内容。

sentences.en: I do know what loop fusion is, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实知道什么是循环融合。

sentences.en: But tell me, what are they both and what is the difference?
sentences.zh: 但请告诉我，它们分别是什么，有什么区别？

sentences.en: So loop fusion is when you take multiple loops and you combine them into a single loop.
sentences.zh: 循环融合是指将多个循环合并为一个循环。

sentences.en: And loop fission is when you take a single loop and split it into multiple loops that iterate over the same index range as the original loop
sentences.zh: 循环拆分是指将一个循环拆分为多个循环，这些循环遍历与原始循环相同的索引范围，

sentences.en: or order of magnitude the same range as the original loop.
sentences.zh: 或者说与原始循环大致相同的范围。

sentences.en: And so you said, you know, you were familiar with loop fusion prior to this conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以你说过，在这次谈话之前你熟悉循环融合。

sentences.en: And that's not surprising because I think that loop fusion is perhaps the more intuitive of these optimizations.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪，因为我认为循环融合可能是这些优化中最直观的一种。

sentences.en: If I take two things that are iterations over n elements and I combine them together,
sentences.zh: 如果我把两个对 n 个元素进行迭代的操作结合在一起，

sentences.en: you know, that's probably a win, especially if the n elements that they're iterating over are the same set.
sentences.zh: 那通常是好事，特别是如果它们迭代的 n 个元素是同一组数据的话。

sentences.en: If the iterations are always accessing the same data, then combining those two loops together, you know, it seems like it'd just be a win, right?
sentences.zh: 如果这些迭代总是访问相同的数据，那么将这两个循环结合在一起，看起来就像是稳赚不赔，对吧？

sentences.en: You're doing, instead of doing, iterating through two n times, you're just iterating through n times.
sentences.zh: 你不需要迭代两次 n 次，只需要迭代 n 次。

sentences.en: But in practice, that's not always the case.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，情况并非总是如此。

sentences.en: And sometimes it's better to have loops be separate
sentences.zh: 有时让循环保持独立更好，

sentences.en: or to even take existing loops that you have and to split them.
sentences.zh: 甚至将现有的循环拆分也是更好的选择。

sentences.en: And the primary reason why you do this
sentences.zh: 你这样做主要的原因是

sentences.en: is to get better locality of reference.
sentences.zh: 为了获得更好的引用局部性。

sentences.en: I'll make the bold assertion that the vast majority of code in the wild is either memory latency or memory bandwidth bound, which essentially means that all of your software
sentences.zh: 我要大胆断言，绝大多数实际代码要么受限于内存延迟，要么受限于内存带宽，这意味着你所有的软件

sentences.en: is pretty much a fancy version of memcopy.
sentences.zh: 几乎都是内存拷贝（memcopy）的高级版本。

sentences.en: The reason for this is because we've gotten very good at building processors that have a lot of compute throughput at a fairly low latency.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，我们已经非常擅长构建具有高计算吞吐量且延迟相当低的处理器。

sentences.en: The problem is getting the data to that execution hardware.
sentences.zh: 问题在于如何将数据传输到这些执行硬件中。

sentences.en: And if you have a ton of data reuse, like, for example, you know, a matrix multiplication,
sentences.zh: 如果你有大量的数据重用，比如矩阵乘法，

sentences.en: which has an O in squared complexity,
sentences.zh: 它的复杂度是 O(n^2)，

sentences.en: and therefore there's a lot of data reuse,
sentences.zh: 因此有大量的数据重用，

sentences.en: then, yeah, you might be able to saturate your execution hardware.
sentences.zh: 那么，是的，你也许能够让你的执行硬件饱和。

sentences.en: But that's not what the majority of applications look like.
sentences.zh: 但大多数应用程序并非如此。

sentences.en: The majority of applications are, you know, I read some sequence of data and I do something with it, and then, you know, I go on and do something else or something like that.
sentences.zh: 大多数应用程序是这样的：我读取一些数据序列，对它做些处理，然后继续做别的事情，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so for most code, the determiner of your performance is going to be your memory access patterns.
sentences.zh: 所以对于大多数代码来说，决定你性能的是你的内存访问模式。

sentences.en: And in particular,
sentences.zh: 特别是，

sentences.en: how efficiently you make use of your cache and your processor's ability to prefetch, et cetera, is going to have a huge impact on application performance.
sentences.zh: 你如何高效利用缓存以及处理器预取数据的能力等，将对应用程序性能产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: I'll give you a simple example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个简单的例子。

sentences.en: Let's imagine that we had two loops.
sentences.zh: 假设我们有两个循环。

sentences.en: And the first loop applies a transformation to one data array.
sentences.zh: 第一个循环对一个数据数组应用转换。

sentences.en: The second loop also iterates over that same array, but it iterates over two other arrays, let's say, as well.
sentences.zh: 第二个循环也遍历同一个数组，但它还遍历另外两个数组。

sentences.en: So the first one accesses one array, the second one accesses three arrays, and one of those is the same as the first one.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个访问一个数组，第二个访问三个数组，其中一个是第一个循环也访问的。

sentences.en: So you might think, okay, well, we should fuse those
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会想，好吧，我们应该融合它们，

sentences.en: because then we only have to access each element of that array, the array that both of them access a single time, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这样我们只需要访问那个两个循环都访问的数组中的每个元素一次，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, here's the problem.
sentences.zh: 现在，问题来了。

sentences.en: When you fuse those loops,
sentences.zh: 当你融合这些循环时，

sentences.en: you might end up disrupting your memory access patterns.
sentences.zh: 你可能会破坏你的内存访问模式。

sentences.en: So one thing that you might end up doing
sentences.zh: 所以你最终可能会做的一件事是，

sentences.en: is you might cause memory accesses that would previously hit in the cache to no longer hit in the cache.
sentences.zh: 你可能会导致原本在缓存中命中的内存访问不再命中缓存。

sentences.en: So pretty much all processors today
sentences.zh: 所以今天几乎所有的处理器

sentences.en: do a pretty good job of prefetching the data that you need into the cache.
sentences.zh: 在将你需要的数据预取到缓存中方面都做得很好。

sentences.en: And if you combine those two loops, now we have to prefetch even more data.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这两个循环结合起来，现在我们就必须预取更多的数据。

sentences.en: And because of that, it's possible that we might have cache misses instead of going through the cache.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，我们可能会出现缓存未命中，而不是通过缓存访问。

sentences.en: So maybe that first loop, which just acts as the one array, maybe that loop was actually really optimal and that loop,
sentences.zh: 所以也许第一个只操作一个数组的循环，那个循环实际上是非常优化的，而且那个循环，

sentences.en: the compiler and the processor were going to always ensure that all of the data was prefetched before each iteration.
sentences.zh: 编译器和处理器总是会确保所有数据在每次迭代前都被预取。

sentences.en: And so it would always run out of cache and it'd be super faSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它总是能从缓存中运行，速度超级快。

sentences.en: But by combining it with the second loop, now you're going to have a cache miss every time.
sentences.zh: 但通过把它和第二个循环结合，现在你每次都会遇到缓存未命中。

sentences.en: And that's going to make your code run slower.
sentences.zh: 这会让你的代码运行得更慢。

sentences.en: And of course, this is even more likely to occur if you have loops that have completely unrelated data that you try to fuse together.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你的循环处理的是完全不相关的数据，而你试图将它们融合在一起，这种情况就更有可能发生。

sentences.en: Because then there's really no data reuse.
sentences.zh: 因为那样真的没有数据重用。

sentences.en: You're just increasing the pressure on the cache of how many different things do I need to fit in the cache with no real reuse between the two.
sentences.zh: 你只是增加了缓存的压力，因为你需要放入缓存的东西太多了，而两者之间没有真正的重用。

sentences.en: But there's another thing that can happen too, which is a larger loop body can have increased register pressure.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一件事也可能发生，那就是更大的循环体可能会增加寄存器压力。

sentences.en: And you should really think about registers as being an even faster type of cache.
sentences.zh: 你应该把寄存器看作是一种更快的缓存。

sentences.en: Let's say you got a processor that has six registers.
sentences.zh: 假设你有一个拥有 6 个寄存器的处理器。

sentences.en: Well, if each loop iteration
sentences.zh: 那么，如果每个循环迭代

sentences.en: only needs six temporary variables for its operations, then that's great.
sentences.zh: 只需要 6 个临时变量来执行操作，那就太好了。

sentences.en: You never have to go to stack memory.
sentences.zh: 你永远不需要去访问栈内存。

sentences.en: Stack memory is always going to be slower than registers.
sentences.zh: 栈内存总是比寄存器慢。

sentences.en: Hopefully, your stack will be in cache.
sentences.zh: 希望你的栈会在缓存中。

sentences.en: It usually is.
sentences.zh: 通常是这样。

sentences.en: But on a processor like a GPU,
sentences.zh: 但在像 GPU 这样的处理器上，

sentences.en: the difference in memory bandwidth and latency between registers and even the first tier of cache is pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 寄存器与第一级缓存之间的内存带宽和延迟差异非常大。

sentences.en: Like on a GPU, spilling to stack is like really not good.
sentences.zh: 比如在 GPU 上，溢出到栈上是非常糟糕的。

sentences.en: You never want to do that.
sentences.zh: 你永远不想那样做。

sentences.en: And that's why there's like a ton of registers on GPUs so that you can avoid doing that.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么 GPU 上有大量的寄存器，这样你就可以避免那样做。

sentences.en: So by combining those two loops,
sentences.zh: 所以通过结合这两个循环，

sentences.en: you might have caused operations that previously did not spill to the stack to have to spill to the stack.
sentences.zh: 你可能导致原本不需要溢出到栈上的操作不得不溢出到栈上。

sentences.en: And that will mean that there is more main memory traffic
sentences.zh: 这意味着会有更多的内存流量，

sentences.en: and also that there are more things that need to be stored in the cache.
sentences.zh: 而且需要存储在缓存中的东西也更多了。

sentences.en: And therefore, there's less room in the cache for the data arrays that you're accessing through.
sentences.zh: 因此，缓存中用于存放你正在访问的数据数组的空间就变少了。

sentences.en: And there's another thing that can happen.
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事可能会发生。

sentences.en: So as I said, the modern processors are pretty good at prefetching all your data.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，现代处理器非常擅长预取你的所有数据。

sentences.en: And one of the ways they do this is they look at your axis patterns and they can figure out linear and strided axis patterns.
sentences.zh: 它们实现这一点的方法之一是观察你的访问模式，并找出线性和跨步的访问模式。

sentences.en: They can be like, oh yeah, you know, like the last like 10 iterations you accessed like this chunk of memory sequentially or you access this chunk of memory with some fixed stride
sentences.zh: 它们会像这样，哦，是的，你知道，过去 10 次迭代你都是按顺序访问这块内存的，或者你以某种固定的步长访问这块内存

sentences.en: between each axis.
sentences.zh: 在每次访问之间。

sentences.en: And so I better just assume that you're going to continue accessing that stream of memory.
sentences.zh: 所以我最好假设你会继续访问那个内存流，

sentences.en: and I'll just fetch where I think the next element's going to be.
sentences.zh: 我会直接预取我认为下一个元素所在的位置。

sentences.en: But if you're accessing a whole bunch of different
